aviso: Datas da cronologia usada pela fonte (tradicional/conservadora; a criação em 4003 a.C. segue Ussher). Antes de ~1000 a.C. os estudiosos divergem muito; as datas não são consenso acadêmico.

eventos.nota: Dan 2:1 says the second year; Jones dates the dream to 604 BC, Nebuchadnezzar's first official year.

eventos.t: The glory of the LORD leaves the Temple
eventos.pt: A glória do SENHOR deixa o Templo
Os caldeus se retiram de Jerusalém

eventos.nota: After the fall of Jerusalem, Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah son of Ahikam governor over the people left in Judah, at Mizpah.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah, sent by Baalis king of the Ammonites, murdered Gedaliah at Mizpah in the seventh month.

eventos.pt: O remanescente foge para o Egito
eventos.nota: Fearing Babylon after Gedaliah's murder, Johanan led the remnant of Judah to Egypt against the word of the LORD, taking Jeremiah and Baruch with them.
Daniel was cast into the den of lions for praying to his God against Darius's decree, and God shut the lions' mouths.
From Cyrus's decree and the first return (536 BC) to the close of the Old Testament record (Nehemiah's second term, Malachi).

eventos.t: Cyrus decrees the rebuilding of the Temple
eventos.pt: Ciro decreta a reconstrução do Templo

eventos.nota: In the seventh month after the return, Jeshua and Zerubbabel built the altar and restored the burnt offerings and the feast of tabernacles, before the Temple foundation was laid.
Ezra read the book of the Law to the assembly in the seventh month; the people kept the feast of tabernacles, confessed their sins and sealed a covenant under Nehemiah the Tirshatha.

eventos.pt: A obra do Templo é interrompida

eventos.nota: Darius I Hystaspis, counted from his first year (521 BC). Jones and Ussher identify him with the Ahasuerus of Esther.

eventos.nota: Mordecai learned of a plot by Bigthan and Teresh to kill King Ahasuerus and told Esther; the plot was recorded in the chronicles.

eventos.t: Haman plots to destroy the Jews

eventos.nota: On the third day of the fast Esther went in to the king unbidden; he held out the sceptre, and she invited him and Haman to a banquet.
Nisan 510 BC, the same Nisan as Haman's decree (Esth 3:12), per Jones's Chart 5; his Appendix F prints 509 BC.
Adar of Darius's 12th year, which falls in 509 BC (Jones).
Artaxerxes I Longimanus, counted from 473 BC when Xerxes made him pro-rex (Ussher, Jones).

eventos.t: Exiles put away their foreign wives

eventos.nota: Chislev of the 20th year falls before the Nisan of Neh 2:1, so Jones dates it to 455 BC.
Jones starts Daniel's 70 weeks (Dan 9:25) from this decree.

eventos.nota: Returning from the king, Nehemiah threw Tobiah out of the Temple chamber, restored the Levites' portions, enforced the Sabbath and dealt with the foreign marriages.
